name: grounded-state-controller-transfer-and-action-v1
claim: A history-grounded material state remains useful under changed known future impedance and can improve constrained action selection over a same-structure snapshot.
unit_of_analysis: physically replayed history pair; controller/action/wait branches stay grouped
datasets: new seeded matched-history Maxwell simulation; previously train-fitted fixed material parameters

splits.name: history
splits.leakage_check: disjoint seed ranges and array hashes; test responses unused for training/early stopping

splits.name: controller
splits.held_out: K=2200 D=45 interpolation, K=4800 D=45 stiffness extrapolation, K=2200 D=110 damping extrapolation
splits.leakage_check: only four training corners in fitting and validation; all known control parameters given to every predictor

baselines.name: gru_contact
baselines.category: controller-conditioned temporal baseline with known contact and actuator

metrics.name: future force RMSE
metrics.rationale: predictive transfer to unseen future controllers

metrics.name: penalized completion time
metrics.rationale: completion time if safe successful, otherwise horizon+1; failures cannot look artificially fast

metrics.name: pair-response-difference NRMSE
metrics.rationale: whether hidden history contrast survives controller transfer

metrics.name: position RMSE
metrics.rationale: command-conditioned motion rather than privileged future-motion input

ablations: contact GRU replaces fixed Maxwell state evolution with a learned sequence closure
falsification_criteria: history does not improve response-contrast error under new controllers
prediction gains produce no action benefit outside tiny boundary subsets
state swaps do not change predicted contrast or decisions
learned history cannot match a competitive short classical observer; no neural-necessity claim allowed
